feedback: If a pupil asserts a symmetry count without checking, have them fold or rotate to confirm or revise it
Connect the number of symmetry lines and the order of rotation to the polygon's equal sides and angles
activities.intendedInsight: Lines of symmetry and order of rotational symmetry are demonstrable facts about a figure, justified by physically folding and rotating rather than by memorised numbers.
learnerActions: Take a cut-out regular hexagon (or other regular polygon) and fold it to find each line of reflective symmetry, counting them
Rotate the polygon over a fixed outline to find its order of rotational symmetry, counting the positions where it maps onto itself
State the result in conventional terms — e.g. a regular hexagon has 6 lines of reflective symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 6 — justified by the folding and rotating, not asserted
Optionally use rotation overlays or fold-line marks to record each symmetry found
activities.title: Symmetry by action: fold and rotate a regular polygon
